after: ## Issues at global, national and local level
alt: The 1996 World Food Summit definition of food security, followed by two tanks: physical scarcity, where the water is not there, and economic scarcity, where it exists but people cannot afford or reach it. Below, subsistence and commercial farming, and virtual water, the water used to produce a product, an idea developed by Tony Allan.
caption: Water can be scarce because it is missing or because people cannot reach it.

alt: India’s July 2023 ban on non-basmati white rice exports kept rice affordable at home but raised prices for families in rice-importing countries. Both want stable prices; the difference is who carries the cost. Other perspectives: smallholders, large farms and food firms, environmental groups and La Via Campesina’s food sovereignty.
caption: A national action that protects one group can shift hardship to another.

alt: A cross-section shows a falling water table: a poorer farmer’s shallow well dries first while a richer farmer drills a deeper well. Agriculture uses about 70% of fresh water withdrawn worldwide (FAO). A chain: cheap pumping lets thirsty crops spread, groundwater falls faster than rain refills it, and a supply problem becomes one of inequality.
caption: When the water table falls, those with the shallowest wells lose first.

alt: A timeline: Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 blocked Ukraine’s Black Sea grain ports; the UN and Turkey brokered the Black Sea Grain Initiative in July 2022; Russia withdrew in July 2023. The general chain: war or drought cuts a harvest, exports fall, world prices rise, and poorer families in importing countries eat less.
caption: A conflict in one region reaches prices in distant local markets.

alt: Rings show one cause reaching three levels in Cape Town, South Africa: a multi-year drought with rising demand nationally, a city warning of Day Zero when taps could be turned off, and households asked from February 2018 to use no more than 50 litres per person per day. Water use fell, rain returned and Day Zero was avoided.
caption: One cause, low rainfall plus rising demand, reached households, a city and a nation.

alt: Five tiles with one shaded show the UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024 estimate that about a fifth of food available to consumers was wasted in 2022, mostly by households. It is strong but an estimate. A fictional fertiliser leaflet claiming farmers always get bumper harvests has a vested interest, a generalisation and no figures; an independent multi-season comparison would be better.
caption: Even a strong source gives an estimate; a weak one gives no evidence at all.

alt: Food waste actions at three levels: SDG target 12.3 to halve waste per person by 2030; France’s 2016 law requiring large supermarkets to offer edible unsold food to charities; and local canteen schemes and school gardens. For the fictional city of Ostley, a donation rule fails because food is ready late and the food bank opens three days a week; adding refrigerated storage removes the barrier.
caption: An action works only if it removes the main practical barrier.
